\subsection{Composable scikit-learn Pipelines: Wine Data}
\label{subsec:cs4-wine}

The wine dataset comprises 178 samples described by 13 chemical measurements,
partitioned into three cultivar classes (59, 71, and 48 samples respectively).
This study demonstrates a different facet of \texttt{fdars}: rather than a
single functional method, it showcases the \emph{composability} of the
\texttt{fdars} scikit-learn estimator layer, which exposes
\nsklearnestimators{} estimators that plug natively into
\texttt{sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline} and \texttt{sklearn.model\_selection.\allowbreak
GridSearchCV} \citep{ramoscarreno_scikitfda_2024}.  Here each 13-measurement
sample is treated as a short functional profile subjected to \emph{functional
preprocessing}; this is not a traditional functional-data interpretation of the
wine measurements, but it exercises the estimator interface exactly as a genuine
functional problem would.

\paragraph{Pipeline.}
We compose an \texttt{fdars} \texttt{FPCATransformer} --- which projects each
sample onto its leading functional principal components
\citep{ramsay_silverman_2005} --- with a vanilla
\texttt{sklearn.discriminant\_analysis.\allowbreak LinearDiscriminantAnalysis}
classifier \citep{preda_saporta_2005}.  Because \texttt{FPCATransformer} obeys
the scikit-learn transformer contract, this heterogeneous pipeline (an
\texttt{fdars} transformer feeding an off-the-shelf scikit-learn estimator)
requires no glue code.

\paragraph{Hyperparameter tuning.}
The number of retained principal components is tuned by
\texttt{GridSearchCV} over the grid $\{2, 3, 5, 8\}$, using 5-fold
cross-validation with a single worker to guarantee deterministic split
ordering.  Mean cross-validated accuracy rises monotonically with the number of
retained components: $0.697$, $0.759$, $0.916$, and $0.961$ for $2$, $3$, $5$,
and $8$ components respectively (Figure~\ref{fig:cs4-gridsearch}).  The best
configuration retains eight components and attains a mean 5-fold CV accuracy of
$0.961$.  Figure~\ref{fig:cs4-scores} shows the FPCA scores of the best
estimator projected onto their first two components, coloured by cultivar; the
three classes form well-separated groups, consistent with the high
cross-validated accuracy.

The analysis is reproduced exactly by \texttt{paper/code/casestudy4.py}, which
computes all reported accuracies live and generates both figures
deterministically (re-running the script leaves \texttt{git diff paper/figures/}
empty).

    Bars show mean 5-fold cross-validated accuracy for each number of retained
    functional principal components; accuracy increases with dimensionality, and
    the best configuration retains eight components (dashed line marks the best
    accuracy).}
  \label{fig:cs4-gridsearch}
\end{figure}
